title: Storage boundary — written update
situation: In a technical discussion, an architect asks why files are outside the relational database. You must write the decision accurately without overstating the evidence.
instructions: Write four sentences separating what the database owns from what the file store owns, and name the risk of merging them.

vocabulary.meaning: the rule that says which store owns a piece of data, so that two stores never both claim to be authoritative
the identifier a database keeps to a file it does not hold, and which becomes stale if the file is removed elsewhere

expectedElements: The boundary between the two stores is drawn explicitly
What the database still owns is named
One consequence of a stale pointer is stated
modelAnswer: Files are stored as objects, while the database keeps only their metadata and a pointer. We separated them because large binaries in a relational table slow every backup and restore, for which the restore timings are our evidence. The limitation is that the pointer and the object are not updated in one transaction, so a pointer can reference a deleted file. A reconciliation job closes that window, and I will document how long the window is.
commonMistakes: Describing the split without saying what the database still owns
Implying that the two stores stay consistent within one transaction
variants: Rewrite the update after a stale pointer has caused a user-visible error.
